docs.private.component: `Private` cuts a SUBTREE out of what a viewer is SHOWN — the visibility twin of `Grippable`'s
permission: privacy cuts what a seat SEES, grip cuts what a seat may MOVE. `access` lists the
viewpoints that may see; the empty list is hidden from everyone, and a hand names its owner to
open it to exactly one.
```ts
import { node, Container, Private, visibleTo } from "game-kit"
const hand = node("northHand",
Container({ layout: "row" }),
Private({ access: ["north"] }))   // the whole hand is north's eyes only
visibleTo(cardInHand, "north")      // true
visibleTo(cardInHand, "south")      // false — the subtree cut
## The view is local, the truth is never written
Privacy is a fact of the TREE, not of the renderer: what changes is only the PROJECTION a seat
is handed. A projection is the consumer's one line — walk the tree and drop what `visibleTo`
denies — and reprojecting the same truth for the same seat returns the same picture, bit for
bit. Whether the denied seat sees NOTHING or face-down backs is the game's choice: a projection
may swap faces before it drops nodes; the atom only says who is denied.
## It cuts a SUBTREE
A private container hides everything in it, so the cards in a hand never carry the atom
themselves. The reverse is ordinary and legal — a private child inside a public container: a
face-down bluff mark on an open desk.
docs.private.hands: Two private hands and your eyes. Pick `seat`: your own hand's cards are on the desk, the other
hand is simply NOT THERE — the cut takes the subtree, so its cards never needed an atom of
their own. The middle pile carries no `Private` and shows for everyone. This scene projects
the denied hand to nothing; a game that prefers face-down backs swaps faces in its projection
before dropping — the atom only says who is denied.
